text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any lightheadedness, visual changes, or nausea immediately before standing up to urinate? I also need to know if you have a history of heart disease or if you were taking any new medications recently.

text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of conditions like diabetes or prostate enlargement that might cause straining or prolonged standing while urinating? Also, were you sitting or standing when the episode occurred, and did you feel lightheaded right before passing out?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Not on any regular medications. Social history: Non-smoker. Drinks alcohol socially. Works as a high school teacher. No recent travel or sick contacts.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the loss of consciousness immediately following urination, the rapid recovery without post-ictal confusion, and the lack of cardiac history, this presentation is classic for a reflex syncope known as micturition syncope. DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition syncope
